body.target_estimand: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), each labelled point in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) has a cohort-common treated conditional mean, and the causal target is \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\), whose value is independent of the replica \(i\). For a joint panel law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), this conditional interpretation and the common-replica equality are asserted only for \(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\).
body.estimand_functional: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), consistency, cohort-common treated-mean replication, and event-date transport identify \(\tau(z_0)=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) for every labelled point \(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications and permits a rule depending on them, selected before only the unknown label. In contrast, every outer random-design MSE or interval rule is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and labelled kernel; this is the convention under which the \(N^{-\lambda}\) donor phase is nondegenerate. The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). The feasible interval uses whole-unit concentration and no calendar-score branch. For every joint panel law, the repaired transfer lemma places its labelled regular conditional kernel, including the common treated mean, in the fixed-query class for almost every query, and only there do causal risk and coverage conclusions transfer. No supremum is taken over panel-specific null conditional values, no lower local modulus is assumed, and no headline result is claimed for \(\lambda>1\).

sampling_model.design: At a fixed admissible query, each exact-design coordinate has conditional density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) almost everywhere and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. The independent-calendar subclass imposes conditional independence only on design dates. These conditions transfer from a joint panel law only on a marginal-conull set of queries.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes. Conditional on the exact design, unit histories are independent across replicas. Their training responses have mean \(m_s(X_{st})\), and every treated replica has the same cohort mean \(\mu_s(z_0)\), invariant under further design conditioning. Full distributions may differ across replicas, and dependence across training dates and the event within one unit remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. The repaired replication clause makes its conditional mean common within cohort. Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; neither centering nor query overlap proves that causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admitted query is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. The donor-location converse uses strict slack \(\delta_0<1/2\); exact fixed-design recovery can be easier when a design site equals the query.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated. Donor folds provide projected means and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort entries. For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative and have unit mass, so whole-unit bounded-range concentration suffices without response mixing, deconvolution, or calendar-score studentization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian convex-class theory links linear-functional minimax risk to a known-experiment modulus; it does not supply the bounded replicated-response and generated-query product experiment used here.
Its estimated-minimizer results use sample splitting and strong convexity, making location error second order rather than a rough-Holder external-query modulus.
Its generated-covariate expansion attaches an estimated coordinate to every training row, unlike the exact historical design and generated event query here.
Its replicated errors-in-variables experiment contaminates every latent training coordinate and requires deconvolution, which is absent under center-only generation.
The classical random-design Holder benchmark supplies ordinary smoothing context but not query-conditional spacing or a generated donor center.
Pointwise local-polynomial minimax theory motivates the anchor smoother but not the bounded product-experiment nearest-site frontier.
Optimal local-polynomial kernels concern ordinary pointwise asymptotic efficiency; the present result establishes only rate constants for a generated-query product experiment.
Random-design sup-norm sharp estimation addresses global loss and design adaptation, not conditional nearest-site recovery at an external generated query.
Classical nonparametric errors-in-variables contaminates all regression covariates, so its deconvolution rates do not govern the center-only design used here.
Generated-regressor asymptotic variance uses smooth semiparametric expansions; it does not cover the nonsmooth rough-Holder query modulus or its minimax converse.
Honest confidence-interval adaptation impossibility motivates fixing the Holder radius and smoothness rather than claiming adaptation across classes.
Ordered moduli characterize confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments; the current interval must additionally cover generated-center error.
Bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals combine worst-case bias and stochastic calibration but contain no external full-covariance donor query.
Dependent-data resampling is not invoked: the repaired theorem uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration and design mixing only for anchor occupancy.
Many-control panel asymptotics motivate cross-unit replication but do not provide the generated-query optimal-recovery frontier.
Dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals address dependent innovations and estimated weights; the repaired interval instead uses unit-history concentration and no calendar-block calibration.
Conformal synthetic-control inference targets robust prediction coverage under a different exchangeability/time-series architecture, not full-covariance generated-query expected-length minimaxity.
The synthetic-control review motivates consistency and data-architecture transparency but does not validate the event-date counterfactual transport equality used for causal identification.
The longitudinal and panel causal-model survey locates the identifying assumptions; it does not derive the conditional generated-proxy minimax or honest-length frontier.

body.tldr: The paper delivers the rough-Holder frontier for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A repaired sampling condition makes each cohort's treated conditional mean common across replicas while leaving their distributions and within-unit training/event dependence unrestricted. The deterministic fixed-design experiment treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications, whereas every outer generated-query estimator and interval is one observable rule chosen before the unknown donor mean; this distinction preserves the \(N^{-\lambda}\) phase. At each admissible query, uniform random-design statements are over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and a disintegration lemma transfers them to each panel law only for almost every query. The nonredundant channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location; the feasible interval concentrates whole unit histories and has no calendar-score branch.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and the former panel-to-kernel argument did not ensure that every treated replica shared the deterministic experiment's cohort mean. A panel regular conditional law is also not defined canonically at query-null values.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths are observed exactly while only the event query is synthesized. The repaired common-mean condition closes the treated-replica transfer without imposing identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. Known-specification fixed-design recovery and unknown-query outer decision theory are kept distinct.
project_justification.fill: The note proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A nearest-site rule attains the deterministic fixed-design scale when \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are known specifications; an anchor/extrapolation rule and a total interval remain single observable procedures chosen before the unknown donor mean. Explicit treated, spacing, and full-covariance donor pairs match the upper rates, and a common-mean disintegration lemma supplies the causal panel bridge almost everywhere in the query.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) studies a known Gaussian convex experiment; here the deterministic bounded product experiment instead has replicated responses, an external full-covariance location coordinate, and fixed specifications \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) known to its decision rule. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, where center error is second order rather than a rough-Holder modulus. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression interval benchmarks, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) study dependent synthetic-control prediction; none supplies an outer generated-query rule, common-treated-mean panel disintegration, or the donor expected-length converse proved here. Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), Low (1997), and Ferman (2021) remain rate, generated-covariate, adaptation, and replication context rather than substitutes for the theorem.
body.interpretation: The repaired fixed-query class makes the cohort treated mean a genuine common label after exact-design conditioning. This is a mean restriction only: it does not homogenize replica distributions or break dependence within a unit history. Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing. A deterministic optimal-recovery rule may use known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); the outer feasible rule may not use \(z_0\), because it must learn that donor mean. Causal interpretation transfers only at almost every realized query.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\) and fixed admissible queries; panel-law statements hold only almost everywhere in the query. The common treated-mean restriction is necessary for the present deterministic-experiment transfer but does not control conditional variances or higher moments beyond boundedness. For \(\lambda>1\), signed local-polynomial weights need additional stochastic stability. Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty, the donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\), and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains untestable. The revised centering condition imposes a common treated conditional mean across replicas and invariance to the exact design, but no identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. Fixed-design minimax rules know \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); outer risk and interval rules are chosen before the unknown \(z_0\) and label. The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division. Panel-law conclusions hold only on a marginal-conull query set; higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants remain outside scope.
